clue.text: Barman starting to hail taxi travelling north

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the opening letter of hail

explanation.surface: A bartender begins hailing a cab heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' looks like a pub worker, but it is a whimsical name for a composer, someone who writes bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach wrote music in bars, so the setter playfully calls the composer a barman.

clue.text: Topless US rock band hires one good ace guitarist at first: 'Snake'

indicators.note: a band that hires players takes them into its line-up, so letters go inside
topless asks us to strip the word top away from the band's name

parts.note: ZZ Top is a Texan rock band
I is the Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for good
A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of guitarist

explanation.surface: A bare-chested American rock group recruits a star lead guitarist nicknamed Snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing TOP from ZZ TOP leaves ZZ; I and G go between the two Zs, and A plus G from guitarist follow. The quotation marks dress 'Snake' up as a nickname, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To zigzag is to wind from side to side, which is how a road or path is said to snake.

clue.text: Tense situations for onychophagists?

parts.note: surface reading: nervy, gripping moments, the kind that keep people on edge
setter's reading: onychophagy is the medical term for chewing one's fingernails, so these people chew theirs

explanation.walkthrough: The plain phrase for a gripping, suspenseful moment is also a literal label for people who chew their nails, which is what onychophagists do.
explanation.definitionFit: A tense, suspenseful contest or film is commonly called by this name, because it makes spectators chew their fingernails.

clue.text: 18s day of victory hidden by trees

definitions.note: refers to 18-down, so the definition is banknotes

indicators.note: something hidden by a screen sits inside it, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees
VE Day is Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: Banknotes from victory celebrations stashed among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 18s sends you to 18-down, BANKNOTES. A fiver is a British five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiver is a five-pound note, so fivers are a particular kind of banknote.

clue.text: Demanded one's nosh, not even on crash diets

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a crash diet is a sudden shock, and crashing smashes the letters into a new order
not even means the even-numbered letters are discarded and the odd ones kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of nosh
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone on a crash diet insists on getting their food.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s of one’s stands for has: I has NS, then the rearranged letters of diets follow. Nosh is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, so insisted and demanded are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: You once put helium into empty tube

indicators.note: putting something into another thing places it inside
an empty word has its contents removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of tube
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: An instruction to pump helium gas into an empty tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the answer as an old form of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic object form of you, used in older English and the King James Bible.

clue.text: Noddy Holder's dairy-free cuppa in evening wear?

indicators.note: this singer is famed for a broad West Midlands accent, so we take the phrase as he would pronounce it

parts.note: a cuppa without milk is a cup of black tea

explanation.surface: A rock singer's milkless brew while dressed for a formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy Holder, singer with the band Slade, comes from Walsall in the Black Country, where the vowel of tea is said much like tie. A cuppa is a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tie is the formal dress code of a dinner jacket and bow tie worn at evening events.

clue.text: Delivered votes to observers

indicators.note: words that are delivered are spoken out, so we go by their pronunciation

parts.note: ayes are votes in favour, as called in Parliament

explanation.surface: Ballots handed over to election monitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayes are yes votes in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs we observe with, so they can be called observers in a playful way.

clue.text: A country jailing 11,000 for life?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a jail locks someone inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: a nation is a country
read as 1 and 1,000: Roman numerals I and M

explanation.surface: A country locking up eleven thousand prisoners for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 11,000 splits into 1 and 1,000, giving the Roman numerals I and M, which go inside NATION after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness or vitality, so it is a synonym for life in the sense of spirit.

clue.text: 'Relligious' rock-and-roll star?

parts.note: religious means holy
the extra l in the misspelling

explanation.surface: A rock-and-roll legend described, with a spelling slip, as devout.
explanation.walkthrough: The misspelling is the wordplay: religious with an extra L becomes holy with an extra L.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddy Holly was a pioneering American rock-and-roll singer of the 1950s.

clue.text: Extremists in Hades finally going brown

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
finally going means the last letter disappears

parts.note: Hades is the underworld, hell
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Radicals in the underworld finally turning brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' suggests zealots, but here it is the two extreme letters of the alphabet, A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel is a light reddish-brown colour, named after the hazelnut and often used of eyes.

clue.text: Shows European film scene being translated

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: vid is short for video, a film
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A European movie scene being dubbed into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: To evidence something is to demonstrate or prove it, so evidences means shows as a verb.

clue.text: Might they be worn by large judges and powerful people?

definitions.text: Might they be worn by large judges
definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: the outsized hairpieces a judge might wear

explanation.surface: A question about what large judges and the powerful might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: British judges traditionally wear wigs in court, so a hefty judge might wear an outsize one.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal term for influential, self-important people comes from the large wigs once worn by men of rank.

clue.text: Loud noise overwhelms head of road sweeper

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a boom is a loud noise

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of road

explanation.surface: A deafening noise drowns out the chief road cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road sweeper' reads as one job title, but the definition is sweeper alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a brush with a long handle used for sweeping floors.

clue.text: Success in Yorkshire, other than returned appliance

parts.note: the win, as said in Yorkshire dialect, is t'win

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: but means except, other than

explanation.surface: A northern triumph, other than a returned household gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire dialect shortens 'the' to t', so 'the win' becomes t'win.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is an old-style washing machine with separate washing and spin-drying drums, a household appliance.

clue.text: Deeply concerned? Share with journalist

parts.note: an interest is a share or stake in a business
ED, short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An anxious question, then an instruction to tell a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition that stretches a little: concerned in the sense of having a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Being interested in a matter means being involved or engaged with it, so deeply concerned fits loosely.

clue.text: Fruit put in the ground, say

indicators.note: say asks us to go by how the words are pronounced

parts.note: to bury is to put in the ground

explanation.surface: Fruit being planted in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A berry is a small, juicy fruit such as a strawberry or blackcurrant.

clue.text: Card game during bathroom break

indicators.note: during means within the span of the words that follow, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Playing cards while popping out to the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: Ombre is a 17th-century trick-taking card game of Spanish origin, rarely seen outside crosswords and period novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old three-handed card game, popular in the 1600s and 1700s and mentioned by Pope.

clue.text: Outlaw king's Eton mess that's used as bread

parts.note: to ban is to outlaw

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellious royal's Eton mess pudding, eaten like bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton mess is a British dessert of strawberries, cream and broken meringue; here mess is the scrambling signal. Bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and a banknote is a piece of paper money, so it is used as bread.

clue.text: Colour on diamonds

parts.note: re means on, concerning
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour on diamonds' looks like a jeweller's phrase; on is the Latin-derived re, as in a letter's subject line.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a primary colour, the shade of blood and of the diamond suit in cards.

clue.text: Talked with religious leader about advent regularly

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the kept letters run backwards
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of advent

explanation.surface: A conversation with a rabbi about the coming of Advent.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit, or rabbit on, is British slang for chattering at length.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech, to rabbit means to talk on and on, so rabbited is a synonym for talked.

clue.text: That person's next in line after, at last, regent

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of regent
an heir is next in line to succeed

explanation.surface: Someone is next in line to the throne after a regent finally steps aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next in line after' reads as one phrase, but after is the link telling us the heir follows the letter from regent.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is used as a singular possessive for an unspecified person, meaning belonging to that person.

clue.text: Car replacement, it's used for exploration in the main

definitions.text: it's used for exploration in the main

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British car
a sub, or substitute, is a replacement

explanation.surface: A replacement car, described as a vehicle for exploring.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is a poetic term for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A minisub is a small submarine used to explore the deep ocean, which poets call the main.

clue.text: Second husband holds end of flower like a plant

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside

parts.note: hubby is an informal word for husband

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of flower

explanation.surface: A second husband holding a flower stem.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter from flower slips in after the first letter of HUBBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrubby means resembling or relating to a shrub, a woody bushy plant.

clue.text: Unruly teens picket a governing body

indicators.note: pickets stand around a workplace, so these letters surround the next one
unruly letters will not stay in order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rowdy teenagers demonstrate outside a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, such as the upper house of the US Congress.

clue.text: Run into large hospital with tip of thumb glowing

indicators.note: into places one piece inside another

parts.note: big means large
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
H is the abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: tip of points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of thumb

explanation.surface: Dashing into a big hospital with a thumb tip glowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means shining or giving off light, so it is a synonym for glowing.

clue.text: Henry quit, Don inhaled, smoking weed

indicators.note: something smoking is fired up and in a state, so the letters are thrown into a new order
quitting means leaving, so that letter departs from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
H is the physics symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry gave up, but Don took a drag on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' and 'smoking' paint a picture of cannabis, but the weed here is a garden one.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered plant that gardeners treat as a weed in lawns.

clue.text: Blue feathers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sad, low in spirits
second meaning: the soft fine plumage of young birds

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a bird's coloured plumage; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Down means depressed as an adjective and soft fluffy plumage as a noun, as in a down pillow.

clue.text: King, losing crown, left noble

indicators.note: in a down entry the crown is the top, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic monarch
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A deposed king leaves a nobleman in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

clue.text: Welcome Penny on board vessels

parts.note: on board conventionally means inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship
hi is a greeting, a welcome
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A greeting for Penny as she boards the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: On board is a crossword convention: the letters go between the two S's of SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are large seagoing vessels, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Satisfy philosopher having his rights taken away

indicators.note: things taken away are removed from what remains

parts.note: Jean-Paul Sartre, the French existentialist philosopher
R is the abbreviation for right, so rights is two of them

explanation.surface: A philosopher stripped of his civil rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rights' sounds like liberties, but it is two R's, which come out of the philosopher's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to satisfy an appetite or desire fully.

clue.text: Drink with tea prepared right

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A drink served with tea made properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the most basic drink, and the noun drink can mean any liquid for drinking.

clue.text: Dancing teacher carries books on ballet move

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within
dancing letters move around and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A dance teacher with books, talking about a ballet step.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet jump in which the dancer rapidly crosses the legs in the air.
